Generous usually means being kind or giving more than expected. So, if the bartender added extra alcohol, is that being generous? Well, on one hand, adding extra alcohol could mean the drink is stronger, which some people might enjoy. Maybe the bartender thought I would like a stronger drink and decided to be generous by adding more. But on the other hand, adding extra alcohol without asking could be problematic. I mean, I might not want a stronger drink, or I might have a limit on how much I drink. Also, if the bartender is adding extra alcohol, is that against any rules or policies? I'm not sure. Also, there's the aspect of responsibility. Bartenders have a responsibility to serve drinks safely. Adding extra alcohol could lead to someone drinking more than they intended, which could be dangerous. So, from a responsible perspective, it might not be the best idea. But then again, if the bartender knows me well and knows that I enjoy stronger drinks, maybe it's okay. It depends on the relationship and the context. In some places, there are rules about how much alcohol can be served in a drink. If the bartender adds extra, they might be breaking those rules, which could have consequences. So, putting it all together, while the intention might be to be generous by adding extra alcohol, it's not necessarily the right thing to do without the customer's consent.
